The Indian Youth Congress faced sharp criticism over a promotional social media video uploaded for its upcoming rally at Ramlila Maidan, which reportedly depicted a young boy secretly filming and clicking photos of young women on a mobile phone without their consent. Following an India Today report highlighting concerns over the normalisation of street harassment and stalking, the video was removed from social media platforms. Responding to the controversy, Indian Youth Congress National President Uday Bhanu Chib stated that recording videos or clicking photos of people without consent is wrong: "Bina bataye video khinchna aur photos khinchna sab galat hai." He added that the video was handled by the organisation's IT cell, explaining that it was not possible to review every proposal beforehand. Chib noted that he would speak with the IT cell team to understand their point of view before deciding on further action, maintaining that one cannot form perceptions or reach conclusions based on a one-sided account.
Cyclone Arnab Nears Andhra Coast; Red Alert Issued, Evacuations Under Way
Cyclone Arnab has intensified into a very severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal and is heading towards the east coast of India. The India Meteorological Department has issued a red alert across Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha, forecasting heavy to extremely heavy rainfall with maximum sustained wind speeds reaching 115 to 125 kilometres per hour, gusting up to 140 kilometres per hour. Landfall is expected along the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. In response to the impending disaster, National Disaster Response Force teams have been deployed across multiple states, while the Indian Navy and Coast Guard remain on standby. Coastal administrations have initiated evacuations from low-lying areas, set up temporary relief shelters, and declared holidays for schools and colleges. Fishermen have been strictly directed to avoid venturing out into the sea as authorities aim for zero casualties.

The inmates staged a medical emergency inside their cell, claiming a prisoner had suffered a seizure. A Very Severe Cyclonic Storm named ‘Arnab’ over the West-Central Bay of Bengal is heading toward the east coast and is expected to cross between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, near Yanam (close to Kakinada), on Wednesday morning (October 28).
According to Dr Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, Director General of the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the cyclone is currently intensifying over the Bay of Bengal, positioned roughly 260–300 km from Visakhapatnam and 300 km from Kakinada.
Landfall & Wind Speed Expectations
During the landfall process on October 28 morning:
Sustained Wind Speed: 115 to 125 km/h, reaching up to 135 km/h.
Peak Gusting: Winds may touch 140 to 150 km/h.
Regional Wind Impact:
South Odisha: 60 to 80 km/h.
North Odisha: 40 to 50 km/h.
Due to the intense wind speeds, severe damage to standing crops (especially paddy), uprooting of large trees, and disruptions to rail, air, and road transit are anticipated.
Red Alert and Local Directives
A Red Alert has been declared across coastal Andhra Pradesh and southern districts of Odisha.
High-Risk Districts in Odisha: Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, and Nabarangpur.
Precautionary Measures: Educational institutions—including schools, colleges, and Anganwadi centres—in these affected Odisha districts have been ordered closed for two days.
Forecast Beyond October 29
The cyclone is expected to weaken progressively after October 29:
Oct 29: System weakens into a Deep Depression.
Oct 30: Further degrades into a Depression.
Rainfall and high winds across Odisha will begin to subside significantly from October 30 onward as the system moves inland and dissipates. Authorities have urged residents in coastal and low-lying areas to stay indoors and follow local administrative guidelines.

Cyclone Arnab has intensified into a very severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal and is moving towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, where a red alert has been issued. According to the 8.30 am update on Tuesday, October 27, the storm travelled west-northwest at 23 kmph over the past six hours. Its sustained wind speed now stands at 140 to 150 kmph, and scientists say it could touch 160 kmph over the sea before making landfall. The system is currently about 400 km south-southeast of Gopalpur, 350 km southeast of Visakhapatnam and 420 km east-southeast of Kakinada.
The cyclone is expected to continue west-northwest until Tuesday evening before turning northwest. It should cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast near Yanam, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, by Wednesday afternoon as a very severe cyclonic storm. Wind speeds at landfall are forecast at 115 to 125 kmph, with gusts of up to 140 kmph. A cyclone alert is also in force for Andhra Pradesh and the adjoining south Odisha coast, and schools have been shut in the affected areas as a precaution.
West Bengal will not see a direct landfall, but the state will not escape the storm’s effects. Winds of 40 to 50 kmph, gusting up to 60 kmph, are expected along the Bengal coast from October 27 to 29. The coastal districts of south Bengal are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rain on October 28 and 29.
The storm has also disrupted rail services. Railways have cancelled the Howrah–Jagdalpur Express (18005) from October 27 to 30, while its return service, the Jagdalpur–Howrah Express (18006), will remain off the tracks from October 28 to 31. The Rourkela–Jagdalpur Express (18107) has been cancelled from October 29 to November 4, and the Jagdalpur–Rourkela Express (18108) from October 30 to November 5. Passengers have been advised to check the latest status with Indian Railways before travelling.

Cyclone Arnab Nears East Coast: Andhra & Odisha On Red Alert, Landfall Likely Tomorrow
Cyclone Arnab has intensified into a very severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal, putting Andhra Pradesh and Odisha on high alert ahead of an expected landfall between Visakhapatnam and Bapatla. The India Meteorological Department has warned of sustained wind speeds reaching 115 to 125 km/h, gusting up to 140 km/h, alongside storm surges and heavy rainfall. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu reviewed preparedness and released 27 crore rupees for cyclone response, directing officials to issue regular alerts and secure reservoirs. Precautionary measures are also underway in Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Telangana, and Puducherry. Disaster management forces, including the National Disaster Response Force, State Disaster Response Force, Navy, and Coast Guard, have been deployed and placed on standby. Police have cordoned off coastal stretches like Kakinada beach, while schools and colleges in several districts have been closed ahead of landfall.
